_doc: A CONTAINER-FLAG SETUP DOCUMENT for the preservation corpus, in canonical
test JSON rather than SVG.
WHY IT EXISTS. `isolated_blending` and `knockout_group` are the Opacity
panel's two page-level blending flags, and they live on Group and Layer
ONLY -- no leaf can carry either. Until 2026-07-28 they were destroyed by
ALL THREE codecs in BOTH ports (coverage gap
`container-blend-fields-survive-no-codec`), so the preservation law could
not range over them: the law's gate snapshots canonical test JSON, and a
field the codec does not emit is a field an edit can destroy in total
silence. They are container fields on exactly the element kinds the law's
T4 BYSTANDER clause is about, which is what makes the hole worth a setup of
its own.
WHY NOT AN SVG, like most vectors' setups. Same reason as
preservation_saturated_bystanders.json: at the time this file was written
the SVG codec carried neither flag either, so an SVG door could not place
one on a bystander. The canonical test JSON is the door that can.
THE SHAPE, and what each id is for:
lyr_flags     -- the enclosing LAYER, both flags true. A container
bystander that every whole-document walk rebuilds.
grp_knockout  -- a GROUP bystander, both flags true. The vector's edit
never speaks to it, but `show_all` walks THROUGH it, so
an implementation that rebuilds a container field by
field to reach the child inside loses both flags here.
That is the Swift copy-site omission class, and it is
the class this setup exists to make visible.
r_inside      -- the leaf inside grp_knockout that gets hidden and then
shown again, so the hide/show nets to zero and the
container walk is the only thing show_all really does.
r_sibling     -- the vector's SUBJECT: nudged, so the run is not
byte-identical and the invariants are not vacuous.
The vector that uses this file names `bystander_fields_present`, so a setup
whose flags silently decayed to defaults on the way IN reds the gate
instead of passing on nothing.
